Dear Principal,

I heard you are thinking about changing the phone rule, and I wanted to write to you before you decide. I think Policy 1 is the better one, where we can bring our phones to school and use them at lunch and free times but they have to be off during class. Taking phones away from the whole school would cause more problems than it would fix, and here is why I think that.

The biggest reason is being able to reach our parents. My mom works until six and sometimes plans change in the middle of the day. Last year my ride fell through and I texted her at lunch and she figured it out before the last bell, so I was not standing in the parking lot for an hour. If phones were banned I would have to go to the office and wait in line behind everybody else who needs the phone, and the secretaries already have enough to do. Also if something bad ever happened at school, like a lockdown or a fire, parents would want to hear from us. I know the school would call them but a text from your own kid is different.

My second reason is that middle school is supposed to be where we learn how to handle things before high school. Nobody in a job is going to have their phone taken away at the door. They are just expected to put it away and do their work. If we never get any practice with that, we are going to be terrible at it later. Policy 1 gives us practice with a real rule attached to it, phone off in class, phone on at lunch. That is a rule an eighth grader can follow.

I know some teachers will say phones are distracting and that people cheat with them and that kids are mean to each other on them. Some of that is true. But Policy 1 already handles the class part, because the phones are off during class. And if somebody is being mean online, banning phones at school does not stop it, they will just do it at home at night where no adult at school can see it at all. I would rather have it happen where a teacher might notice.

The last thing is that a total ban is really hard to enforce. People will still bring phones, they will just hide them in their hoodie pockets and check them in the bathroom. Then teachers have to spend their time searching for phones instead of teaching, and good students who forgot to leave it home get in trouble for nothing. With Policy 1, the rule is clear, and if someone uses their phone in class you can take it for the day. Punish the people who break the rule instead of everybody.

Please choose Policy 1. It keeps phones out of class, it keeps us connected to our families, and it treats us like people who can learn to be responsible.

Sincerely,
An eighth grade student

If I couldn't have my phone at all I would be standing outside the school at 3:15 not knowing what was going on. I think a lot of parents would be upset if you banned them completely for that reason alone.

The second reason is that the ban would not really work. This is the part I think adults don't always see. If you say no phones at school, kids are still going to bring them. They will just keep them in their pocket and use them in the bathroom or under the desk, and then teachers have to spend their time being phone police instead of teaching. My cousin goes to a school with a total ban and he says people are on their phones constantly, they are just sneaky about it. But with Policy 1 there is no reason to sneak, because you can just wait twenty minutes until lunch. Rules that people can actually follow get followed way more than rules that are impossible.

Some kids use their phones to listen to music while they eat, or look something up, or text their mom that they got a good grade. That is not hurting anyone's education. And honestly, taking away the one break we get all day doesn't make us better students, it just makes us more annoyed.

I do want to say I understand the concerns. Phones in class are a real problem and I have seen people watching videos during a lesson, which isn't fair to the teacher or to the rest of us. That is why I think Policy 1 should have a real consequence attached to it. If your phone goes off or comes out during class, it gets taken until the end of the day, and if it happens again your parents have to come get it. That way the rule has teeth. Students would learn pretty fast that the deal is, you get your phone at lunch, but class time is class time.

Policy 1 gives students a reason to follow the rule and gives teachers a clear line to enforce. I hope you will choose it.

Thank you for reading my letter and for listening to what students think.

Sincerely,
A 8th grade student

If I did not have my phone I would be standing in front of the school for an hour not knowing what was going on. There is a phone in the office, but last time I tried to use it there was a line of six kids and the secretary was on a call, and by the time I got through my mom had already left work. Another reason is that lunch and free time are our time, not class time. We are not learning during lunch. We are eating and talking. If someone wants to look something up, or show their friend a video of their dog, or check the score of a game, that does not hurt anyone. I understand that phones are a distraction in class, and honestly they are. I have seen kids in my science class hiding their phone under the desk and then having no idea what the homework was. That is exactly why Policy 1 says phones have to be off during class. It fixes the actual problem instead of punishing everybody all day for something that only matters for about six hours of the day.

Also, I think a total ban would be really hard to enforce, and it might make things worse. If phones are not allowed at all, kids are still going to bring them. They will just hide them better. Then teachers have to spend time searching people and arguing about it, and students start lying to teachers about it, which is not good for anybody. When a rule is impossible to follow, people stop taking the rules seriously in general. But if students know they get their phones at lunch, there is a lot less reason to sneak. You are giving us a fair trade instead of a fight.

One more thing. We are in eighth grade and next year we go to the high school, where almost everyone has a phone. If we never get any practice putting the phone away when we are supposed to, we are not going to magically learn how in September. Learning to control it is a skill, kind of like learning to manage your own homework time. Policy 2 does not teach us anything about self control. It just removes the phone and hopes for the best.

I know some people will say that phones cause drama and cyberbullying, and that is true sometimes. But most of that happens at night and on the weekend anyway, when the school cannot control it either way. Banning phones from 8 to 3 does not stop that. What helps is teachers and counselors talking to us about it, which our school already does.

Thank you for reading this and for asking what students think. I really do believe Policy 1 is the smarter choice, because it keeps classrooms focused and still treats us like people who can be trusted a little.

Sincerely,
A concerned eighth grader
